title: Gated rollout decider lab notes and rollback cheatsheet (Jan 2027)
content:
Objective:
This is a compact lab-style note for deciding gated-rollout thresholds, scheduling a quiet window, and a condensed rollback cheatsheet. For the upcoming platform release (RLSE-3421) we want a reproducible decision flow for moving from canary -> gradual -> ramp, plus a one-page fallback checklist for on-call and shift leads.

Scope and constraints:
- Target audience: release engineers, on-call SRE, platform owners, release leads.
- Goal: keep production latencies under 95th-200ms SLO during ramp; fail closed to safer variant if signal degrades.
- Constraint: limited Dedicated GPU capacity the week of 2027-01-11 -> need to rely on multi-variant routing and backfill policies.

Quick decision heuristics (gated-rollout decider):
1) Canary window (0-1% traffic, 30m min): must pass all smoke + cumulative error budget < 10% of baseline.
2) If canary OK -> gradual 5% increments every 60 minutes, each increment requires 2/3 signals OK: latency, error-rate, token-cost delta.
3) If any increment fails -> hold for 30 minutes + triage. If failure persists -> rollback to previous variant.
4) Hard stop: if 95th-latency > 2x baseline OR user-visible error-rate spike > 0.5% absolute -> immediate rollback.

Preflight checklist (must be green before canary):
- [ ] Release artifact uploaded to registry and hash verified (sha256 matched).
- [ ] Canary config pinned in routing service (route: platform-canary-v2).
- [ ] Telemetry: RR-views (latency, p50/p95/p99), errors (4xx/5xx split), model-quality signals (sanity prompts) are streaming to dashboard.
- [ ] Alert rules set for temporary thresholds (canary mode).
- [ ] Load-replay prepared for 1% test traffic (tickets: RLSE-3498).
- [ ] Nightly backup snapshot completed and rollback image validated.
- [ ] On-call roster and escalation ladder confirmed for quiet window.
- [ ] Stakeholders notified (Product/CS/Support) and accept monitoring windows.

Quiet window planner (candidate windows):
- Prefer low-traffic weekday windows for minimal user impact.
- Proposed window: 2027-01-12 02:00-06:00 UTC (backup teams available).
- Secondary: 2027-01-13 22:00-02:00 UTC (APAC-friendly).
- Note: Quiet window must be clarified in the rollout calendar and announced 48h prior in #release-ops and to paging lists.

Rollout calendar (compact timeline):
- T-72h: Final smoke tests, freeze marketing messages, confirm capacity reservations.
- T-48h: Stakeholder announcement + Slack ping.
- T-24h: Tag release, schedule canary orchestration.
- T-0 (start quiet window): Deploy canary (0.5% traffic) -> start 30m smoke.
- +1h: If canary OK -> 5% traffic. Observe 60m.
- +2h: 10% traffic. Observe 60m.
- +3h: 25% traffic. Observe 60m.
- +4h: 50% traffic. Observe 60m.
- +5h: Ramp to 100% if all signals stable.

Signal definitions (explicit):
- latency.p95: baseline + 20% tolerated for canary; for ramping use absolute thresholds (e.g., 200ms absolute).
- errors.total_rate: compare native 5m rolling delta vs baseline; alert if relative increase > 30% and absolute > 0.1%.
- cost.tokens.per_request: watch for delta > 10% (indicates accidental longer generations).
- model-quality: run 5 prompt sanity set every 15m; fail if >2 regressions.

Fallback matrix (short):
- Minor regression (non-user-facing errors, small latency drift): pause ramp, reduce batch sizes, enable KV-cache warmup, retry increment in 30m.
- Medium regression (increased 4xx/5xx but degraded to part of customers): divert 20% traffic to stable variant, escalate to eng on-call.
- Severe regression (user visible errors or data corruption risk): immediate route all traffic to stable variant, trigger rollback runbook.

Rollback cheatsheet (one-page actionable):
1) Decision: On-call + release lead declare "rollback now" in Slack and incident channel.
2) Commands (platform CLI):
   - Check current variant: redwoodctl routes describe platform-service --env=prod
   - Switch routing back: redwoodctl routes set platform-service --variant=stable --weight=100 --env=prod
   - Confirm: redwoodctl routes describe platform-service --env=prod | grep stable
3) If routing fails -> emergency DNS toggle to fallback LB (ops-only, see ops-dns-runbook).
4) Post-rollback: run smoke tests, validate telemetry, create incident timeline entry, tag commit with rollback note.

Release notes draft (to be copied to release page):
- Highlights:
  - Deploy platform inference runtime v2.14.0 with improved kv-cache warmup and attention kernel tuning (expected 8-12% p95 latency improvement on long sequences).
  - Add routing policy for multi-variant serving that allows weighted fallbacks by region.
- Migration notes for integrators:
  - No API changes expected. If you use streaming hooks, please validate tool-call semantics in the canary environment.
- Known issues (tracked):
  - RLSE-3498: intermittent token accounting discrepancy on dedicated nodes under high-burst; mitigation: throttle burst policy until patch.
  - Temporary: some internal metrics tags will change ("runtime_kernel" -> "kernel_version"); dashboard queries need update.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm quiet-window coverage for support in APAC (ask Aisha).
- [ ] Validate canary prompt set includes a negative-case that catches hallucination regressions (Marco to add 3 prompts).
- [ ] Decide whether to enable auto-fallback to quantized variant when latency crosses threshold (tradeoff: cost vs quality).

Post-rollout retro items to collect (short list):
- Telemetry gaps: which signals were noisy and need higher sampling?
- Rollout cadence: did 60m increments lead to faster detection than 30m?
- Communication: did stakeholders receive timely updates?

Field notes (handy reminders):
- If rollback happens, keep the postmortem short and timeline-first. Playbook link to reuse: Confluence Release Playbooks page.
- When in doubt: prefer user-visible safety (route to stable) over chasing cost savings.
- Quick CLI snippet to capture current routing state: redwoodctl routes export platform-service --env=prod > /tmp/routes-before-rollback.json

Appendix: quick links and references:
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/987
- Canary tickets: RLSE-3498 (load replay), RLSE-3421 (release epic)
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/Release+Playbooks
- Slack: #release-ops archive -> thread ts:1672305600.000200

Notes to self: keep this doc short; strip to two pages for runbook handoff. Use this as the single source during the quiet window, and paste the Release Notes Draft into the release page once ramp finished.
